definitions.explanation: A severe misfortune or disaster, often with connotations of fate or supernatural causes. More literary and dramatic than everyday words for disaster.

examples.japanese: {厄災|やくさい}が{降|ふ}りかかる。
{厄災|やくさい}から{身|み}を{守|まも}るためにお{祓|はら}いをする。
examples.english: To perform a purification ritual to protect oneself from calamity.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}は{人類|じんるい}にとって{最|もっと}も{大|おお}きな{厄災|やくさい}の{一|ひと}つだ。
examples.english: War is one of the greatest calamities for humankind.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}は{過去|かこ}に{何度|なんど}も{厄災|やくさい}に{見舞|みま}われてきた。
examples.english: This region has been hit by calamity many times in the past.

notes:
A literary word for calamity or disaster, often carrying connotations of fate, divine punishment, or forces beyond human control. Commonly encountered in literature, historical writing, fantasy/game contexts, and formal speeches. In everyday conversation, {災害|さいがい} or {災難|さいなん} are more typical.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {厄災|やくさい}が{降|ふ}りかかる: for calamity to befall
- {厄災|やくさい}に{見舞|みま}われる: to be struck by calamity
- {厄災|やくさい}を{もたらす}: to bring about disaster
- {厄災|やくさい}を{払|はら}う: to ward off calamity
- {厄災|やくさい}から{逃|のが}れる: to escape from disaster

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {災害|さいがい}: disaster — the standard neutral term, used for natural disasters and emergencies
- {災難|さいなん}: misfortune — personal-scale bad luck or trouble
- {惨事|さんじ}: tragedy, catastrophe — emphasizes the horrific nature of an event
- {天災|てんさい}: natural disaster — specifically caused by nature
- {厄|やく}: bad luck, unlucky year — relates to superstition about certain ages

FORMATION:
{厄|やく} (misfortune, bad luck) + {災|さい} (disaster) — combines two characters both relating to calamity.
